perspective:
From Harold Padilla’s subjective perspective, he has access to:

- He is Harold Padilla, a project manager. Arthur Begum is a police officer and a friend he relies on for advice/support.
- He feels frustrated and anxious because his project team seems unmotivated and project progress is suffering.
- He arranges to meet Arthur at a local coffee shop.
- At the coffee shop, Harold tells Arthur that his team seems completely unmotivated and it is affecting progress; he is at his wit’s end.
- Arthur tells him motivation can be tricky and asks whether he has tried understanding what drives each team member individually.
- Harold admits he has focused on project goals/deadlines, not personal motivations.
- Arthur advises that people need to feel valued and understood personally, and suggests one-on-one conversations.
- Harold says he will try it, thanks Arthur, and feels hopeful and relieved. He believes Arthur’s advice will help.
- Harold meets with his team and proposes quick one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each person.
- Team Member 1 says that could be helpful. Team Member 2 says they are open to it.
- Harold says he will schedule time with each of them and wants to make the project a success together.
- Later, Harold notices the team still is not responding well. He feels disappointed and worried about the project’s future.
- Harold tells Arthur he tried the suggestions but the team still is not responding well.
- Arthur tells him there may be deeper issues: personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that he may need to dig deeper.
- Harold says he had not thought of that, asks what kind of issues Arthur means, then decides to set up another round of meetings. He thanks Arthur.
- Harold feels determined and focused. He believes there may be underlying team issues he has not addressed.
- Harold holds one-on-one meetings and asks team members to share concerns or problems.
- Team Member 1 tells Harold there has been tension between a few team members, and it is affecting work.
- Harold thanks Team Member 1 and says he will look into resolving the conflicts.
- Team Member 2 tells Harold they feel overwhelmed by the workload and struggle to stay motivated when constantly stressed.
- Harold says he understands, will see if tasks can be redistributed, and says their well-being is important.
- Harold feels optimistic and empowered. He believes addressing individual concerns will improve team performance.
- Harold tells the team they will have regular feedback sessions and team-building activities to create a more supportive environment.
- Team Member 1 says that sounds great and will help them work better together.
- Team Member 2 says they agree and it is good that their concerns are being addressed.
- Harold says he is glad, asks them to work together to make the project a success, and says their input and well-being are crucial.
